q: 1. Construction site planning is concerned with
options: minimize the chances of wastages, deterioration and losses
maximize the safety and execution of work
explain: Construction site planning encompasses site layout, safety management, waste minimization, material handling, and progress monitoring to ensure smooth project execution.

q: 2. Construction site planning mainly depends upon the
explain: Effective site planning must account for ground and space conditions, the specific engineering nature of the project, and the required construction methodologies.

q: 3. The types of construction in which more equipment are used, is known as capital intensive while the construction in which more human labours are used, is called
explain: Projects relying predominantly on manual workforce rather than heavy machinery or automated plant equipment are classified as labour intensive.

q: 4. During storage of cement, the bag of cement should be kept......cm apart from the walls.
explain: Standard site storage specifications mandate keeping cement stacks at least 30 cm (12 inches) away from exterior walls to prevent moisture absorption from walls.

q: 5. Earned value analysis is used for comparing of the project
explain: Earned Value Analysis (EVA) integrates scope, schedule, and cost metrics to compare actual work completed (earned value) against the planned schedule baseline.

q: 6. A project is
options: a large dam constructed across a river to earn profit
any job involving many people and large money
a work of major importance involving huge men and investment
an organized team work to achieve a set task within the time limit
explain: By definition, a project is a temporary, organized endeavor undertaking unique tasks with a defined beginning, end, scope, and resource constraint.

q: 7. Policy is
options: a rule or a set of rules never to be violated
a definite rule along which one has to proceed
a procedure for preparing the project report
a set of broad guidelines stipulated by management
explain: Policies serve as overarching guidelines established by executive management to direct decision-making and organizational actions.

q: 8. The expected project duration in CPM follow
explain: Due to the Central Limit Theorem, the total project completion time in critical path network calculations follows a normal distribution.

q: 9. The relation between jobs of a particular type and various durations they have consumed for completion is expressed by
explain: A frequency distribution curve plots observed activity durations against their occurrence counts to evaluate historical activity variations.

q: 10. The constraint in case of resource smoothing operation would be
explain: In resource smoothing, the critical path and total project completion time are fixed constraints; floats of non-critical activities are utilized to smooth demand without delaying the deadline.

q: 11. In resource leveling the main constraint would be
explain: Resource leveling is a resource-constrained technique where maximum available limit of resources cannot be exceeded, often extending total project duration.

q: 12. A construction schedule is prepared after collecting
explain: Drafting an accurate construction schedule requires complete work breakdown quantities, labor productivities, equipment capacity ratings, and sequence of operations.

q: 13. The main principle of an organization, is
explain: Sound organizational structure relies on core management principles including clear scalar chain, delegation of authority, effective span of control, and unity of command.

q: 14. The main advantage of line organization is
options: ability to quick decision at all level
explain: Line (scalar) organization provides direct vertical authority, enabling swift decisions, clear individual accountability, and strong operational discipline.

q: 15. The main disadvantage of line organization is
explain: Line organization suffers from key weaknesses such as lack of expert specialization, rigidity, potential concentration of power, and vertical communication delays.

q: 16. Military organization is known as
explain: Line organization is the oldest and simplest form of organizational structure, often referred to as military organization due to its direct, top-down chain of command.

q: 17. Line organization is mostly suitable for
explain: Because it lacks specialized technical staff departments, pure line organization is best suited for small scale or simple operational work.

q: 18. Types of organization used in construction industry is
explain: Direct line organization (or line and staff variations) is predominantly utilized on basic construction sites to maintain clear site discipline and accountability.

q: 19. Frederick W. Taylor introduced a system of working known as
explain: F.W. Taylor developed functional foremanship (functional organization) to group operations by technical specialization rather than pure scalar hierarchy.

q: 20. The salient feature of functional organization, is
options: each individual maintains functional design part
work is properly planned and distributed
explain: Functional organization relies on technical specialists to plan, supervise, and control specific operational functions according to standards.

q: 21. Line & staff organization is mostly suitable for
explain: Line and staff organization combines scalar command with expert advisory staff, making it ideal for complex, large-scale engineering endeavors.

q: 22. In histogram, more prominent will be the differences in heights between the bars if
explain: A wider variation (larger range) across class intervals creates distinct variations in frequency count heights on a histogram plot.

q: 23. Gantt chart indicates
options: balance of work to be done
comparison of actual progress with the scheduled progress
explain: Gantt charts plot activity progress bars against time, allowing project managers to directly compare actual site progress against planned schedules.

q: 24. The diagrammatic representation of the activity of the entire project is called
explain: Project activities can be visually charted using network models, process flow diagrams, or control tracking charts depending on analysis goals.

q: 25. In a bar chart the length of horizontal lines for activity A and B are 2 cm and 4 cm respectively. Which one is correct about the activity A & B?
options: activity 'B' need more duration for completion
activity 'A' need more duration for completion
completion time for activities 'A' and 'B' are same
explain: In bar charts, the horizontal axis represents time duration; thus, a longer line directly corresponds to a longer duration required for completion.

q: 26. Bar charts are considered suitable for
explain: Due to their inability to clearly show detailed dependencies and critical paths, bar charts are primarily suited for smaller or minor projects.

q: 27. Which types of network was first developed for planning of any project?
explain: The Gantt bar chart was developed around 1900-1915, making it the pioneer graphical scheduling tool preceding milestone charts and network methods like CPM/PERT.

q: 28. On a bar chart the various activities of a project are shown by
explain: Activities in a traditional Gantt chart are plotted along the vertical axis, with their duration spans depicted by horizontal bars.

q: 29. Jobs going ahead of schedule are conveniently shown in
explain: By overlaying actual completion bars against planned timeline bars, a Gantt chart clearly displays activities running ahead of schedule.

q: 30. The upper portion of horizontal bars in a bar chart indicates
options: total duration for completion of an activity
progress of work in the specified time
due duration for the completion of an activity
explain: In conventional progress bar charting, one portion of the bar represents scheduled duration while the adjacent/upper track indicates actual progress achieved.

q: 31. Henry Gantt developed the bar chart technique in
explain: Henry Gantt devised his historical system of project progress charts around 1900–1915.

q: 32. Milestone charts are developed in
explain: Milestone charts were introduced around 1940 as an improvement over plain bar charts to mark key events or completion points.

q: 33. Gantt Bar chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart explicitly plots individual activities (vertical axis) against time or duration (horizontal axis).

q: 34. The limitations of bar chart are
explain: Bar charts fail to show interrelationships between tasks, cannot account for probabilistic activity variations, and lack explicit variance controls.

q: 35. The weakness in bar charts is
options: uncertainty in duration for various activities
the sequence of activities is not very clear
explain: Key deficiencies of bar charts include hidden interdependencies, lack of sequence logic between non-consecutive bars, and no risk/uncertainty factor.

q: 36. A milestone chart
options: shows the interdependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but not in a logical sequence
explain: While milestone charts highlight important achievements along a timeline, they still lack explicit logical link arrows showing task interdependencies.

q: 37. The interrelationship between the functional elements of a programme is achieved through
explain: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) decomposes a project systematically into manageable work packages and elements to show structural connections.

q: 38. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt bar chart is structured with project tasks listed on one axis and time intervals plotted along the perpendicular axis.

q: 39. A drawback of bar chart is
options: it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
all the activities represented are independent of each other
sequence of activities is not clearly defined
it is not possible to judge whether the activity is ahead or behind the schedule.
explain: The critical limitation of a standard bar chart is that it does not show logical dependency linkages or critical activity sequences.

q: 40. Time and progress chart of a construction is known as
explain: Bar charts, Gantt charts, and Critical Path Method (CPM) networks all serve as methods for planning and tracking time and progress in construction.

q: 41. The amount of time required performing any event in case of PERT should be ..... CPM.
explain: In theoretical event-based networks, events themselves represent points in time (instantaneous), taking zero or negligible time compared to activity-oriented CPM tasks.

q: 42. PERT technique of network analysis is useful for
explain: PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is suited for non-repetitive, R&D, or complex projects where activity durations are uncertain.

q: 43. An event is
options: a definite position of an activity
explain: An event represents a specific milestone or point in time marking the accomplishment of a stage (start or end) of an activity.

q: 44. PERT means
options: pertinent programming related to a project
explain: PERT stands for Program Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 45. PERT is
explain: PERT focuses primarily on key project milestones and completion points, making it an event-oriented technique (whereas CPM is activity-oriented).

q: 46. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: Waiting consumes time (e.g., concrete curing time), which qualifies it as an activity in network calculations even if it doesn't require direct labor.

q: 47. In PERT technique, completion of an activity is called
explain: The ending point of an activity arrow in a network diagram is called its head event, representing the activity's completion.

q: 48. The benefit of the PERT network is taken by the management in
options: readjusting the time to meet the target
explain: PERT allows managers to plan schedules under uncertainty, coordinate concurrent tasks, and analyze trade-offs to meet target dates.

q: 49. Which of the following time estimate is related to PERT?
explain: PERT uses three probabilistic time estimates for every activity: Optimistic ($t_o$), Most Likely ($t_m$), and Pessimistic ($t_p$).

q: 50. The event which act as head as well as tail for different activities is, called
explain: An intermediate event that marks the finish (head) of preceding activities and the start (tail) of succeeding activities is called a dual-role event.
